open_obligations: Check that Smit et al.'s Multi-Persona matches Liang et al.'s MAD prompts.
Note agreement intensity is a prompted target, not a measured agreement rate.
Check whether Liang et al.'s disagreement levels map onto Smit et al.'s X values.
in.other_title: Agreement intensity: prompting debaters to agree X% of the time
in.rationale: Liang et al. propose MAD with two debaters in a 'tit for tat' state and a managing judge. Smit et al. add an agreement-intensity prompt ('agree with the other agents X% of the time') applied to Multi-Persona, which they describe as derived from Liang et al., and to other MAD systems.
in.scope: proposed EXTENDS: controlling disagreement in multi-agent debate, from fixed tit-for-tat prompting to a tunable agreement intensity

text: The authors propose MAD, in which two agents argue their positions in a 'tit for tat' state and a judge monitors and manages the debate to obtain a final solution. They argue that in MAD one agent's distorted thinking can be corrected by others, its resistance to change complemented by others, and each agent receives external feedback, so MAD is less susceptible to the causes of DoT.
title: MAD framework: two tit-for-tat debaters and a judge that manages the debate
